name: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5 — Moderate Baseline
description: Selected technical controls from NIST Special Publication 800-53 Rev. 5 — the catalogue used by FedRAMP, FISMA and CMMC. This file maps host-hardening rules to the AC, AU, CM, IA, SC and SI control families.

controls.name: Account management
controls.desc: Manage system accounts: no extra UID 0, default Guest disabled, lockout policy on failed attempts, audit logon events.

controls.name: Least privilege
controls.desc: Limit accounts and processes to the minimum privileges required. UAC, mandatory access control, no privileged containers, restricted SUID set.

controls.name: Unsuccessful logon attempts
controls.desc: Limit consecutive invalid logon attempts via SSH MaxAuthTries, account lockout policy and continuous monitoring of failed logins.

controls.name: Remote access
controls.desc: Remote access mechanisms must be authenticated and encrypted. Key-based SSH only, root SSH disabled, RDP requires Network Level Authentication, X11 forwarding disabled.

controls.name: Event logging
controls.desc: Audit subsystem must be active and configured to capture security-relevant events including authentication, privileged commands and PowerShell script blocks.

controls.name: Time stamps
controls.desc: System clocks must be synchronized to a reliable source so audit records can be correlated across hosts.

controls.name: Audit record generation
controls.desc: Audit records must be generated for the events identified in AU-2. Failed logons must be visible to monitoring.

controls.name: Configuration settings
controls.desc: Establish and enforce a hardened baseline: MAC, kernel hardening (IP-forward, redirects, RP-filter, ASLR, SUID dumpable), Windows hardening (UAC, SMBv1 off, LLMNR off, auto-login off).

controls.name: Least functionality
controls.desc: Disable unused, insecure services and protocols. SMBv1, LLMNR, and WDigest credential storage are removed; only required ports respond.

controls.name: Identification and authentication (organisational users)
controls.desc: Each user authenticates with a unique credential. Public-key SSH, password complexity, minimum length and account lockout applied.

controls.name: Authenticator management
controls.desc: Authenticator content protected: modern password hashing (yescrypt / sha512), shadow file readable only by root, WDigest plaintext store off, complexity policies enforced.

controls.name: Boundary protection
controls.desc: Host firewall active on all profiles; IP forwarding off; reverse path filter on; ICMP redirects ignored.

controls.name: Transmission confidentiality and integrity
controls.desc: Strong TLS protocols and ciphers, valid certificates, mandatory SMB signing — all transit traffic protected.

controls.name: Cryptographic protection
controls.desc: Approved cryptographic algorithms only; weak protocols and legacy credential stores disabled.

controls.name: Protection of information at rest
controls.desc: BitLocker (Windows) or equivalent disk encryption to protect data should the device be lost, stolen, or repurposed.

controls.name: Flaw remediation
controls.desc: Security patches applied, no reboot pending, automatic updates available where supported, no Known-Exploited / critical / high CVEs outstanding.

controls.name: Malicious code protection
controls.desc: Anti-malware enabled with real-time scanning and current signatures (Microsoft Defender on Windows; equivalent enforcement on Linux via MAC and file-permission hygiene).

controls.name: System monitoring
controls.desc: Audit subsystem, failed-login monitoring, anti-malware real-time protection and Windows audit logon events provide continuous visibility.
